business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Internet - DTC Brand Webstore

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Swiss Confederation and the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 27 April 2009; entered into force 13 April 2010)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Art. 697j of the Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220) [obligation of non-listed stock companies to identify and record beneficial owners at the 25% threshold]; Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (Money Laundering Act, SR 951.0), Arts. 2, 3, 8a and 11; Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0), Arts. 305bis and 305ter; FINMA AML/CFT circular guidance on beneficial ownership and enhanced due diligence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity document of each proposed shareholder, director, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or civil registry office in the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority in the country of origin or Swiss consular legalization for non-Hague members

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation / commercial register extract of the ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar or official commercial registry in the parent entity's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus certified English translation if the original is not in an official Swiss language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incumbency or good standing listing current directors and beneficial owners of the parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent or official corporate registry in the parent entity's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the Swiss incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or consular legalization; German, French, or Italian certified translation may be required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter evidencing source of funds for the share capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent bank or financial institution in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature and apostille if requested by the Swiss AML compliance officer; otherwise direct bank-channel confirmation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed shareholders, directors, officers, authorized signatories, and any beneficiary at or above the 25% threshold must be screened before incorporation and on an ongoing basis against (i) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (ii) the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) sanctions and embargo measures; (iii) relevant EU and US OFAC sanctions lists; and (iv) reputable public and premium PEP databases. If any person is a Politically Exposed Person as defined in Art. 2a of the Money Laundering Act, enhanced due diligence under Arts. 6 and 8a MLA is mandatory, including documented source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification, independent Swiss bank introduction, and adverse media checks.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Central Business Name Index (www.zefix.ch) operated with the cantonal commercial register offices; electronic filings via the e-gr.ch portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Commercial register entries are made in the official language of the registration canton (German, French, Italian, or Romansh). The company name may be in any language using Latin script, but a transliteration or official-language version may be required by the cantonal register. The name must not be misleading as to the legal form, business purpose, or association with public authorities, and must comply with the commercial naming rules of the Swiss Code of Obligations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended once for an additional 90 days by written request to the cantonal commercial register office before expiry. If the name is rejected, the applicant must file a written administrative objection with the cantonal commercial register office within 10 days of notification. If the objection is denied, a further administrative appeal may be filed with the competent Cantonal Administrative Court, and thereafter, on questions of law, with the Federal Supreme Court of Switzerland.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not acceptable as the sole registered seat. The Aktiengesellschaft must maintain an actual administrative head office in Switzerland in accordance with the Swiss Code of Obligations. Third-party registered-agent services and virtual-office addresses can satisfy correspondence and legal-process requirements, provided the agent maintains an operational physical office in the canton and the company keeps complete corporate records, registered share register, and UBO documentation at or accessible from that address. For a low-risk DTC e-commerce activity, no industry-specific substance beyond normal corporate administration is required.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection is approximately 5-10% for a non-licensed, low-risk DTC e-commerce company. Inspections may occur in the context of money-laundering investigations, commercial register compliance audits, or consumer-protection/supply-chain enforcement actions. Banking counterparties performing independent AML onboarding reviews may also conduct physical site verification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR, SR 220), Articles 629-646 (incorporation and share capital), Articles 626-627 (Articles of Association), Article 716b (board appointments); Federal Act on the Commercial Register (HRegV, SR 221.411); Commercial Register Fee Ordinance (GebV-HReg, SR 221.411.7).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug (Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug), operating under the supervisory authority of the Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized deed of incorporation (Errichtungserklärung) together with the Articles of Association (Statuten), filed electronically as an application for registration (Anmeldung zur Eintragung), followed by publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Nominal share capital of at least CHF 100,000 is mandatory; no less than CHF 50,000 must be fully paid up in cash before registration and held in a blocked escrow account at a Swiss bank or authorized finance company, verified by a bank confirmation for release only after commercial registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the subscribed share capital of CHF 100,000, divided into 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100 each, be and is hereby approved, issued, and fully subscribed by the founding shareholder, with CHF 50,000 paid up through the blocked capital deposit account; (2) that the registered office be established at the Company's address in the Canton of Zug and the executive secretary be instructed to file the incorporation application with the Commercial Register; (3) that [Name] be appointed managing director with sole signatory authority, and [Name] be appointed chairman of the board of directors; and (4) that the board be authorized to open bank accounts, obtain tax and social security registrations, and execute all ancillary incorporation instruments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name reservation and trade name clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug through the national Zefix portal; Federal Institute of Intellectual Property (IPI) for trade mark screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Query the Zefix company index to confirm that the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and that the business purpose is lawfully covered by the Aktiengesellschaft legal form. File a name availability request with the Zug Commercial Register Office before drafting the statutes.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name in full legal form
Identity document of the applicant or founding agent
Drafted business purpose clause (Zweckartikel)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts with an existing entry, amend the name to achieve distinctiveness; obtain an official prior name-check confirmation from the registry to reduce the risk of rejection at the notarial stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of minimum paid-up capital on a blocked bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank or Swiss finance company in the Canton of Zug acting as escrow depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a reference-money deposit account in the Company's name and deposit at least CHF 50,000 with a blocking instruction (Zeichnungssperre) providing that funds are released only to the directors after full commercial registration. Obtain a depositary confirmation (Bankbescheinigung) identifying the account holder, deposit amount, and blocking condition.
required_dossiers: Bank account application signed by designated board members
Draft Articles of Association containing the capital clause
Passports or identity cards of all subscribers
Beneficial ownership declarations under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries incomplete AML documentation, resubmit certified identity and corporate documents; if the bank refuses the mandate, select another licensed bank and re-execute the deposit, documenting the transaction in the notarial deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the deed of incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (Urkundsperson) appointed by the Canton of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary together with all subscribers; adopt the Articles of Association, execute the capital contribution declarations under Article 630 OR, and confirm the absence or approval of pre-incorporation commitments. The notary verifies the identity, legal capacity of the founders, capital payment documentation, and the lawfulness of the company name and purpose.
required_dossiers: Passports or identity cards of all founding shareholders
Draft notarial deed of incorporation
Articles of Association signed by all subscribers
Statement on the intended use of paid-up capital
Declarations of the elected board members accepting office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies omissions or defects, prepare a notarial addendum or re-execute the deed; registration cannot proceed until the notarial deed is complete and formally certified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic submission of the registration application to the Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug (Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the fully executed deed, Articles of Association, supporting declarations, and the registration application through the approved electronic notary interface. The application must include the list of shareholders, the board composition, the authorized signatories, and the bank confirmation for the paid-up capital.
required_dossiers: Certified notarial deed of incorporation
Certified Articles of Association
Bank depositary confirmation of the CHF 50,000 blocked deposit
Identity documents of all directors and authorized signatories
Certified specimen signature cards for each authorized signatory
List of shareholders with shareholdings and capital contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The registry issues a formal deficiency notice (Fristwarnung) granting at least 10 days to cure defects. Upon cure, registration proceeds; if the application is refused, appeal to the Cantonal Supervisory Authority and subsequently to the Federal Administrative Court within 30 days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration entry and publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB), operated by the Federal Office of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Commercial Register records the Company and issues the enterprise identification number (UID). The entry is published in SHAB within two business days; legal personality of the Aktiengesellschaft arises on the registry entry date, not on the publication date.
required_dossiers: No additional dossiers are required; publication is executed administratively by the registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SHAB publication contains data errors, file a correction request with the Commercial Register, which is processed with a nominal administrative fee. If a third party contests the registration under Article 537 OR, submit evidence of capital payment and follow the judicial objection procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration mandatory registrations with tax, social security, and accident insurance authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV), VAT Division; OASI Compensation Office (AHV-Ausgleichskasse) Zug; SUVA Accident Insurance; Office of Economic Affairs and Labour (AWA) of the Canton of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply within 30 days for the VAT identification number, register the Company with the OASI compensation office for employees, and obtain mandatory accident insurance with SUVA. No business license is required for pure internet retail; a cantonal trade notification is filed with AWA only if the Company operates a physical warehouse or fulfillment space in Zug.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract (Handelsregisterauszug)
FTA/VAT registration application form
Estimated turnover and accounting method declaration
Social security employer registration documents
SUVA accident insurance application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT application is queried, resubmit with cash-flow projections and turnover estimates above the CHF 100,000 threshold; if AWA requires a trade notification, supply the site plan and storage description. Failure to register with FTA or the OASI compensation office exposes the Company to statutory default assessments and interest.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Office of Economic Affairs and Labour (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit, AWA) of the Canton of Zug
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating license is required for ISIC 4791 internet retail under Swiss law; formation through the Commercial Register is the sole authorization. A cantonal trade notification (Meldebescheinigung) is conditionally required only for physical warehouse or fulfillment premises exceeding 200 m².

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Cantonal Environmental Protection Office (Amt für Umwelt des Kantons Zug) acting under the Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt: not listed in Annex I of the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV); an EIA is not required for a webstore or small distribution warehouse. Registration is triggered only if warehousing or fulfillment floorspace exceeds 2,000 m² or solvent-based processing is introduced.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater; sanitary sewage connected to the municipal sewer network in compliance with the Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV, SR 814.201). Packaging waste must be returned or recycled under the Packaging Ordinance (VVVO). VOC emissions from cleaning or printing operations, if ever introduced, must comply with LRV (SR 814.318.142.1) Annex 5 thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: obtain the Zug fire-police completion certificate (Feuerpolizeiliche Abnahme) and register the premises with the cantonal building insurance. Structural safety: provide a certified static load assessment for the office or warehouse floor where loads exceed 4 kN/m². Occupational clearance: pass the AWA labor inspectorate inspection under ArGV 3 covering emergency exits, lighting, ventilation, sanitary facilities, and rest areas, and confirm SUVA accident insurance coverage for all workers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC), Bern. Online portal: ESTV eServices portal (https://www.estv.admin.ch), Swiss VAT e-business portal (eService für Unternehmer), and Swiss Central Business Name/UID register.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A domestic Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (AG) is automatically assigned a Swiss Business Identifier (UID, CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx) upon registration in the Commercial Register; this UID is the principal tax reference for federal, cantonal, and communal tax authorities. VAT registration is filed with ESTV via electronic registration in the Swiss VAT eServices portal, using the UID, extract from the Commercial Register, articles of association, governing body details, and expected taxable turnover figures. For non-established foreign enterprises, a simplified Swiss VAT registration procedure is available through ESTV, with an obligation to appoint a Swiss tax agent only in defined cross-border situations; the VAT identification number (MWST-Nr / IDE / TVA) is issued in electronic form after completeness review.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law does not operate a US-style check-the-box election; legal-form classification under the Swiss Code of Obligations is controlling for direct tax. The relevant optional mechanisms are: (i) VAT small-business election under Art. 10 MWSTG/Art. 10 LTVA allowing otherwise non-taxable suppliers with worldwide turnover below CHF 100,000 to voluntarily register for VAT; (ii) the optional patent box regime and R&D super-deduction under the Swiss Tax Reform and AHV Financing Act 2019; (iii) the qualified participation deduction for dividends/capital gains on qualifying participations; (iv) cantonal tax statuses/rulings for holding, domicile, or mixed companies remain abolished but are grandfathered for limited transitional periods. Hybrid mismatch rules apply under Art. 57a-57e DBG (VStG) only as a defensive provision; there is no elective hybrid-mismatch opt-out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / Mehrwertsteuer MWST / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide taxable turnover excluding VAT, under Art. 10(1) MWSTG/Art. 10(1) LTVA. For Swiss-resident DTC e-commerce retailers, turnover from zero-rated exports is counted in determining whether the CHF 100,000 threshold is reached. Separate statutory rules apply to non-established suppliers of electronically supplied services and low-value distance sales, which may trigger Swiss VAT registration with specific de minimis conditions and special facilitation rules as set out in ESTV guidance.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate a continuous transaction control (CTC) system, real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory e-invoicing clearance, or digital stamping obligation. The Swiss QR-bill (QR-Rechnung) is mandatory for all domestic payment slips issued to Swiss payers, serving as a structured payment instrument rather than a tax clearance. E-invoicing is permissible and commonly used in PEPPOL and FacturaSuite formats, with no prior tax-authority approval. Taxpayers must issue invoices containing the mandatory Swiss VAT invoice content prescribed by Art. 26 MWSTV/Art. 26 OLTVA and retain books, invoices, and supporting documentation for at least 10 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Switzerland to a destination outside Switzerland are zero-rated if the supply is made to a foreign purchaser, ownership passes to the purchaser, and the goods are actually transported out of Switzerland by an authorized export procedure; Swiss export documentation must evidence the customs release. In addition, certain services directly connected to exported goods or international transactions may qualify for zero-rating under the Swiss VAT law. For online DTC sales via Shopify, each shipment must be accompanied by a valid Swiss electronic export declaration and transport proof; delivered-at-place terms or equivalent Incoterms must not contradict the export evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Validated electronic Swiss export declaration (via the Swiss Single Window, containing the MRN or national export registration number, goods description, quantity, value, customs office and date of release)
Commercial invoice and, where applicable, underlying purchase order or sales contract
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR/House Waybill as applicable showing the shipped quantity and destination outside Switzerland
Proof of payment / bank credit statement indicating receipt of the export proceeds, or inward remittance certificate where requested by the tax authority in audit
Customs transit or export proof such as the National Transit System (NCTS) declaration text, export list, or customs certified exit confirmation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss Federal and cantonal tax authorities examine export zero-rating claims on a risk-based and transaction-level basis. If an export declaration, transport proof, or consideration evidence is false, incomplete, or contradicted by payment data, the tax authority retrospectively recharacterizes the supply as taxable in Switzerland and assesses Swiss VAT at the standard rate, together with default interest and late-payment interest. Intentional tax evasion relating to VAT or customs duty is punishable under the Swiss Federal Act on Administrative Criminal Law (VStrR) and the VAT Act with monetary fines of up to at least twice the amount of tax evaded, and in aggravated cases further criminal penalties; negligent underdeclaration triggers monetary penalties. Customs offences may result in separate confiscatory fines and forfeiture of goods. There is no Swiss statutory deadline or obligation for repatriation of FX proceeds; therefore the zero-rating audit focuses solely on lawful export proof and the economic substance of the cross-border transaction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland applies a fully convertible currency and capital-control-free regime for both current and capital transactions. Residency-based limitations are absent; cross-border fund transfers are unrestricted. Profit remittance in the form of dividends or loan repayments is lawful without foreign-exchange permission. Only the Swiss anticipatory withholding tax (35%) applies to distributions to non-residents unless mitigated by an applicable double taxation treaty. CHF floats freely and may be traded without central bank authorization, although SNB monetary policy interventions can influence exchange-rate conditions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Swiss law imposes no mandatory surrender, repatriation timeline, or conversion ratio on export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained in foreign currency abroad, converted at will, or settled in EUR, USD, or any freely tradable currency. Banks require only a generalized transaction-purpose statement for anti-money-laundering record-keeping under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA). No SNB balancing or reporting obligation exists.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI (Electronic Money Institution) accounts without FINMA authorization are not viable as the main treasury rail for a Swiss AG. They lack Swiss banking license status and therefore do not obtain FINMA prudential supervision, Swiss deposit insurance, or local settlement finality. Feasibility rating: LOW for primary liquidity; they may be used only as auxiliary collection channels with automatic daily sweeping into a FINMA-supervised Swiss bank account. Any payment institution holding client funds for more than 60 days in Switzerland triggers a licensing requirement under the Banking Act or FinTech Ordinance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss banks must conduct identity verification of all beneficial owners and signatories under AMLA. For a cross-border e-commerce AG, the standard mandate is a physical presence of the beneficial owner and at least one managing director at a bank branch or before a Swiss notary/public official. Some Tier-1 Swiss banks permit remote onboarding using SwissID or qualified electronic signatures for low-risk clients, but a virtual interview by bank personnel is still compulsory in nearly all cases. A fully frictionless remote account opening without any human interview is practically unavailable for a corporate entity engaged in multi-jurisdictional card-acquiring e-commerce.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume payment-aggregator settlements from Stripe, PayPal, and Shop Pay with commingled consumer collections
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the active Shopify store URL, product catalog, consumer target-market list, pricing and refund policy, monthly settlement statements from each payment gateway, VAT/registration certificates, and a projected cash-flow model breaking down gross sales, gateway fees, and net proceeds. Include a written explanation of the payment flow and a source-of-funds declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex ownership with non-Swiss shareholders or discretionary trust structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the full notarized company statutes, current commercial-register excerpt, shareholder register, a signed AMLA beneficial-owner form for each ultimate human owner, identity and passport copies, proof of address, source-of-wealth documentation, and a transparent corporate-organizational chart from the AG up to the ultimate individual shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No physical operational office in the canton of registration and only remote fulfillment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply the registered-office lease or sublease agreement, Swiss contact service and mandatory mail-forwarding arrangement, a business-plan narrative showing how logistics are executed through Swiss third-party fulfillment providers, inventory-holding agreements, and prior corporate tax and VAT filings to demonstrate substantive Swiss nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Elevated rate of chargebacks, refunds, or subscription-cancellation patterns characteristic of digital commerce
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver chargeback-monitoring and refund-standard operating procedures, terms of service and cancellation policy, proof of Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) for card transactions, monthly reconciliation reports, and a compliance attestation signed by the board confirming compliance with consumer-protection regulations in target jurisdictions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 with explicit purpose code for equity injection ('SHARES' or 'CAPITAL INCREASE') or shareholder loan ('INTRA-GROUP LOAN'; SWIFT format may also employ 'LOAR'). Funds must be received on a FINMA-supervised commercial bank account in the name of CH_AG. Supporting documentation must include board minutes approving the capital increase or loan, certified share register excerpt after entry in the Swiss commercial register, and a source-of-funds bank reference. No Swiss National Bank approval is required, and no mandatory exchange-surrender or notification applies.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational payment streams use SWIFT MT103 wire transfers with exact beneficiary account details and an enumerated invoice reference. For high-value or initial trade relationships, use commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) with Incoterms 2020 and presentation documents including commercial invoice, bill of lading or proof of shipment, and inspection certificates. Dividend and profit remittances require SWIFT MT103 plus a dividend-payment voucher from the board and, if reduced withholding tax is sought, the Beneficial Owner Form. All outbound disbursements must be matched against underlying trade contracts, customs records, and VAT reporting where applicable.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot contracts and outright FX forwards for USD/CHF, EUR/CHF, and GBP/CHF
Currency futures traded on regulated exchanges (CME, Eurex)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM): approval of the annual financial statements (Jahresrechnung), annual report, election or re-election of the Board of Directors and of the independent proxy, and grant of discharge (Décharge) to the Board of Directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the Aktiengesellschaft; minutes retained in the company minute book, with Board composition changes subsequently filed at the cantonal Commercial Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the business year (Art. 699 para. 2 Swiss Code of Obligations); calendar-year AG therefore due by 30 June of the following year, unless special circumstances justify a later date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No administrative strike-off exists in Switzerland; however, directors face civil liability and criminal exposure under the Swiss Code of Obligations for failure to convene the AGM, and persistent non-compliance may enable shareholders or creditors to petition a court for judicial dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return of the AG, covering federal direct tax and cantonal and communal direct taxes, accompanied by the approved annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration of the canton of registered office, acting simultaneously for the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / AFC) under the Federal Direct Tax Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing date set by the applicable cantonal tax law, commonly between 31 March and 30 June of the year following the tax year; extensions are available only upon timely application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest accrues on unpaid taxes from the statutory due date; late-filing penalties and procedural fines are imposed, and intentional under-declaration may trigger criminal tax proceedings under Art. 175 et seq. of the Federal Direct Tax Act and equivalent cantonal provisions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT settlement declaration (Mehrwertsteuer-Abrechnung) — annual settlement period for eligible small businesses, or six-monthly or quarterly settlement for higher-turnover taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / AFC), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of the VAT settlement period (Art. 71 VAT Act); an annual settlement ending 31 December is accordingly due in February or March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on overdue VAT; procedural penalties for late or incomplete submission; enforced collection of arrears; and criminal VAT sanctions for deliberate failure to declare taxable turnover

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer wage declaration (Jahreslohnausweis) for statutory social security (AHV/IV/EO/ALV), family allowances (FAK), occupational pension (BVG) and mandatory accident insurance (UVG)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Employer's compensation office (Ausgleichskasse), occupational pension institution, and accident insurer (e.g., SUVA or private insurer)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due by 31 January of the year following the calendar year for the AHV annual wage statement; insurer-specific deadlines apply for UVG and BVG annual payroll declarations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on unpaid social security contributions, administrative fines under AHVG/UVG/BVG, personal liability of directors for unremitted employee contributions, and criminal proceedings for false wage declarations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register mutation filing after the AGM for the annual re-election or re-appointment of the Board of Directors and any resulting change in registered officers or powers of signature; also used for any other corporate record change during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) with mandatory publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Without undue delay (unverzueglich) after the relevant corporate resolution or event, in accordance with the Commercial Register Ordinance; there is no annual public return, and registration is effective only upon entry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors acting before registration may be exposed to personal liability for unregistered acts; the Commercial Register may refuse or impose corrective measures, and false or materially inaccurate declarations may result in administrative penalties and criminal consequences

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An ordinary (full) statutory audit is mandatory if the AG or its group exceeds, in two consecutive financial years, at least two of the following thresholds (Art. 727 Swiss Code of Obligations): balance-sheet total of CHF 20 million; turnover of CHF 40 million; annual average of 250 full-time employees. Otherwise, a limited audit (Review) is required, unless the AG validly opts out of any audit by not exceeding, in two consecutive years, at least two of the following thresholds (Art. 727a CO): balance-sheet total of CHF 2 million; turnover of CHF 2 million; annual average of 10 full-time employees, and all shareholders consent to the opt-out
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory financial statements must comply with the accounting provisions of the Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957–963b CO), which constitute the Swiss statutory accounting framework; IFRS Accounting Standards and Swiss GAAP FER may be applied voluntarily, and IFRS is effectively required for issuers listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: An AG with registered shares must maintain a share register (Aktienbuch) recording the names and addresses of all shareholders and their shareholdings. If the AG has issued bearer shares, it must additionally maintain a register of beneficial owners under Art. 697i CO. Switzerland currently does not impose a central UBO registration filing or an annual UBO confirmation statement; the Board must update the internal registers continuously as transfers occur and ensure the register is accurate as at the AGM. The share register may be inspected by shareholders and, to the extent provided by law, by competent authorities. Any capital or shareholder change reported in the annual tax return to the cantonal tax administration is subject to assessment by the tax authority
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners (required only if bearer shares are issued)
Register of Directors and Statutory Officers (Board and authorised signatories)
Minute Book (minutes of the Annual General Meeting and Board of Directors)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 – 5,000 per year for Swiss fiduciary or corporate services providing registered office, mail handling, statutory register maintenance and corporate-secretarial coordination
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – 7,000 for a limited statutory audit (Review) of a small e-commerce AG; USD 0 if the Art. 727a CO opt-out is valid; ordinary full statutory audit typically ranges from USD 15,000 to USD 40,000+ depending on group size and complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal tier: 8.5% on profit after federal tax, equal to 7.83% effective on pre-tax profit. Combined federal, cantonal and communal headline burden for an AG domiciled in Zug: approximately 11.9% of pre-tax profit (Zug benchmark; municipalities vary 11.9%–12.9%; higher in Geneva, Zurich, Basel-Stadt where total reaches 18%–21%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: TRAF/STAF 2020 package: patent box relief (up to 90% of qualifying IP profit, Zug fully applies the federal maximum), R&D super-deduction up to 150% of eligible labour and research costs, notional interest deduction (available in certain cantons, currently not Zug for ordinary equity). Additional relief: participation exemption (Art. 69 DBG) eliminating federal/cantonal tax on qualifying dividend and capital gains, and tax-neutral capital contribution reserves (Art. 60 lit. e DBG) allowing tax-free distribution of paid-in share premium. No statutory tax holidays or preferential regimes exist for a DTC retail sales company at federal level; Zug applies a comparatively low ordinary rate and modest capital tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Unified federal-cantonal corporate income tax return ('Steuererklärung juristische Personen', federal form code 707 combined with the Canton of Zug corporate form) filed jointly with the Zug Tax Administration (Dienststelle Steuern Zug) and the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV). Electronic filing via the accredited secure portal 'SwissTax' (e-filing module for legal persons) with XML import from commercial accounting packages; VAT under a separate ESTV portal (VAT return quarterly/annually, not part of the income tax return).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Tax computation is based on the preceding fiscal year; prepayments of corporate income tax, capital tax and withholding tax instalments are collected quarterly by the canton based on prior-year assessments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six (6) months after the end of the fiscal year for both the federal and the Zug cantonal return; for a calendar-year entity the statutory deadline is 31 May of the following year. Extensions are routinely granted upon written request up to 30 September (federal) and 31 October (Zug). Where the AG is audited by an external tax expert, the canton normally accepts filing by the extended deadline without penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from goods and services before deduction of discounts and returns; for a Shopify DTC operation this includes the full customer selling price less platform payment-provider fees only if they are contractually borne as cost, with platform/transaction fees shown separately.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare only revenue attributable to the Swiss AG's permanent establishment/effective activity in Switzerland; intra-group cross-border sales must be priced at arm's length and supported by documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Z2 / Box 2 – Warenaufwand (cost of goods sold, COGS)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Purchasing cost of inventory, inbound freight, customs duties, packaging and write-downs of inventory to net realisable value; includes costs of third-party logistics directly attributable to the sold goods.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party purchases from a foreign group entity must be benchmarked under an approved method (CUP or TNMM preferred); keep contemporaneous evidence of comparable margins.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross wages, employer social security contributions (AHV/IV/EO/ALV), pension contributions to a Swiss tax-recognised pension fund (BVG), accident insurance and other statutory personnel costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Salaries of non-resident employees must be subject to Swiss payroll withholding if a Swiss PE exists; management fees paid to a foreign related entity for services of the shareholder are deductible only if genuinely rendered, adequately documented and at arm's length, otherwise treated as constructive dividend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-depreciable amounts on tangible fixed assets (declining balance) and intangible assets (straight-line); useful lives correspond to ESTV depreciation tables (e.g. machinery 5 years, software 4 years, furniture 8 years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Amortisation of purchased e-commerce intangibles (website, customer lists, brand) must reflect an arm's-length acquisition price; a non-resident arm's-length charge is accepted only with a valuation report.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Z5 / Box 5 – Finanzerfolg (financial income and expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, currency gains/losses, banking charges, interest on shareholder loans and other treasury results.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loans from non-resident shareholders are treated as hidden equity where the debt-to-equity ratio is excessive (thin capitalisation safe harbour generally 1:6 for holding, 1:3 for operating companies); the excess portion of interest is disallowed and reclassified as taxable constructive distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net profit before income taxes per the statutory annual accounts, adjusted for non-deductible expenses, provisions, and tax-exempt participation income; this figure forms the basis for federal, cantonal and communal profit tax after the separately declared tax-exempt participations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The computed taxable profit of the Swiss AG is subject to regular Switzerland profit tax at both federal and local level; treaty relief does not apply to income tax of a resident company, only to withholding tax on cross-border distributions and payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assets per the statutory Swiss balance sheet (Swiss GAAP FER or OR-compliant accounts); used by Zug for capital tax assessment (Zug capital tax is assessed on paid-in capital, statutory reserves and retained earnings at approximately 0.04% combined municipal/cantonal rate).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders' contributed capital (share premium) must be recorded in a separate capital contribution reserve to benefit from tax-free repayment under Art. 60 lit. e DBG; an entry showing retained earnings instead of reserve creates Swiss withholding tax exposure on later distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of all profit distributions, interest on bonds or profit-participating loans, and constructive dividends (e.g. non-arm's-length transactions, hidden profit distributions) paid or credited to shareholders during the reporting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Swiss AG must deposit the 35% federal withholding tax with ESTV within 30 days of the distribution or, for constructive distributions, within 30 days of the tax assessment becoming final. A non-resident shareholder wanting the treaty rate must file the proper DTA refund application; where the deposit is not made, the directors become personally liable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: disciplinary fine of up to CHF 10,000 per non-compliant return (Art. 174/175 DBG) plus daily surcharge as determined by the canton; if the return remains unfiled, the tax authority estimates the taxable base by discretion and may order a formal default assessment with interest at 4.5%–5% p.a. Audited tax evasion (intentional or negligent omission): fine of up to three times the evaded tax, and, for aggravated cases with falsified books, imprisonment up to three years and/or a fine. Voluntary disclosure before criminal discovery still mitigates but does not eliminate administrative penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) levied at source on any dividend or profit distribution of a Swiss AG, including distributions out of statutory reserves and constructive dividends stemming from non-arm's-length transactions (Art. 4 VStG). The withholding is refundable only upon the shareholder's application; for Swiss resident corporate shareholders the tax is fully creditable; for non-residents it is final unless reduced under an applicable DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA rate (generally 15% for portfolio dividends, 5% for a shareholding of at least 10%, and under some treaties 0% for qualifying participations): (i) the non-resident shareholder must obtain an official tax residence certificate ('Ansässigkeitsbescheinigung' / TRC) from the home state tax authority, valid for the calendar year and not older than the end of the previous year; (ii) before the dividend payment, the beneficiary may request relief at source by submitting the TRC and a completed ESTV Form 823 (request for reduced-rate relief) to the Swiss agent or directly to ESTV; (iii) if full 35% was withheld, the shareholder must file a refund application within the statutory three-year period after the end of the calendar year in which the tax was withheld (Art. 33 VStG, using Form 825 for dividends) together with the TRC and a statement certifying beneficial ownership; (iv) the refund is accelerated where the foreign tax authority certifies through the Mutual Agreement Procedure. The DTA relief applies only to the beneficial owner; a conduit set up without substance will be denied relief under the MLI Principal Purpose Test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory source withholding: royalties — 0% (Switzerland does not impose any domestic withholding tax on licence fees, therefore payments for trademarks, software copyrights or patents to non-residents are paid gross); interest — 0% for ordinary bank interest and trade finance interest; however, interest on bonds and profit-participating loans issued by a Swiss AG may be subject to the 35% withholding tax. Under DTAs, royalty withholding rates are typically 0% (or a maximum of 5%–10% in older treaties) and interest rates 0%–10% (e.g. 0% under the China–Switzerland DTA for interest paid to a bank with a majority government participation; 10% standard rate otherwise). Fine exceptions apply to royalty-like payments from Swiss situs intellectual property and to excessive related-party interest that is recharacterised as a constructive dividend, in which case the full 35% is levied and the treaty rate may be denied.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory TP documentation (Local File and, if applicable, Master File) is triggered once the Swiss company exceeds the small-enterprise exemption: more than two of the following three criteria are met — (i) more than 50 full-time employees; (ii) annual turnover above CHF 20 million; or (iii) balance-sheet total above CHF 10 million (per the Swiss Code of Obligations test applied by the ESTV's TP circular of 2012). For the Shopify DTC brand operating through an AG with turnover crossing CHF 20 million, the Local File must contain the group overview, benchmarking study, and arm's-length justification for intra-group services, royalties and loans; a Master File is required for groups with global consolidated turnover above CHF 50 million. Failure to submit contemporaneous documentation reverses the burden of proof and enables the tax authority to apply an income adjustment and a penalty surcharge.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply a formal Economic Substance Regulations regime as in the UAE, but imposes substantive requirements through (i) anti-abuse clauses in domestic law (Art. 21 DBG denial of tax advantages for purely artificial arrangements), (ii) the OECD/MLI Principal Purpose Test incorporated into treaty relief, and (iii) the ESTV's practical substance test for holding, domiciliary, pure finance and mixed companies in cantons (including Zug) that grandfather transitional privileges. A Swiss AG holding the e-commerce brand and collecting worldwide Shopify revenue must have, in Switzerland: an operative board with actual meeting minutes, a real business address, an independent economic decision-making process, bank accounts, payroll for personnel performing substantive functions, and no flow-through of capital to investors without commercial justification. Absent such substance, the tax authorities may deny residence benefits, reallocate income to the beneficial owner's jurisdiction, disallow treaty protection for the 35% withholding tax, and impose the full 35% withholding on deemed distributions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – deliberate under-declaration of e-commerce revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional misstatement or omission of Shopify sales, website revenues, PayPal/Stripe receivables or worldwide customer turnover in the Zurich/Zug tax return, or booking of personal expenses as business costs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to three times the amount of the evaded federal and cantonal tax (Art. 175 DBG), plus default interest of 4.5%–5% p.a. on the unpaid principal from the statutory due date, plus cantonal administrative penalties of the same magnitude. The unpaid tax remains collectible with compound interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The board of directors and the mandatory Swiss accounting representative personally bear penalty liability under Art. 181 DBG as the persons who caused the infringement. Directors may be individually fined, their travel abroad restricted where criminal tax proceedings are opened, and their private assets garnished to cover the company's fiscal debt if the company is insolvent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Fraud – falsified books and forged evidence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creation of false invoices, double bookkeeping, destruction or concealment of accounting records, falsification of balance-sheet documents, or signed false declarations accompanying the tax return, in furtherance of tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of up to three years and/or a monetary penalty (Art. 176 DBG), with no statutory minimum; in aggravated cases the prison sentence can be combined with a fine of up to three times the evaded tax; additional cantonal criminal sanctions apply simultaneously. The company itself faces liability under Art. 102 Swiss Criminal Code for organisational defects.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or cause the filing of falsified returns are prosecuted personally and may be sentenced to imprisonment; they receive a criminal record, are barred from holding Swiss board positions, and face extradition where the home state requests them. Criminal asset seizure, travel bans and entry into the Schengen Information System are routinely ordered by Swiss investigating judges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Constructive Dividend / Hidden Profit Distribution (Transfer-Pricing Override)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying supra-normal management fees, royalties or interest to a non-resident related entity, or transferring the e-commerce brand and customer list to a foreign group company at a price below arm's length, thereby shifting profit out of Switzerland.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority re-adds the excess payment to taxable profit and simultaneously deems a constructive dividend; the Swiss AG must deposit 35% withholding tax on the constructive distribution within 30 days of the final assessment. The re-assessment can reach back 10 years and triggers TP re-documentation with a 5–10% surcharge on the adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approved or benefited from the non-arm's-length transaction are personally and severally liable for the entire avoided withholding tax under Art. 12 VStG; where the company cannot pay, the director's personal assets are directly seizable. In cases of fraudulent intent, criminal sanctions for tax fraud apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell-Company Pact / Absence of Economic Substance in Switzerland
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Swiss AG serves solely as a mail-box or invoice-splitting vehicle: no employees, no office, no operational decisions, board members are non-resident nominees, revenues pass through without real functions, or the company claims treaty benefits while being managed from abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of the domicile status may result in: (i) disqualification from treaty protection so that the 35% Swiss withholding tax becomes final and non-refundable; (ii) full taxation of the deemed liquidation of the Swiss entity upon transfer of assets abroad; (iii) retrospective profits reallocation to the state of effective management with double taxation; (iv) administrative fine under the anti-abuse provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and beneficial owners are treated as responsible persons: they may be ordered to appear before the Zug tax authority, be subject to asset freezes in Switzerland, and face personal liability for all unpaid taxes and penalties. Repeated abuse triggers criminal prosecution for qualified tax evasion with imprisonment, and the Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering is applied to confiscate the funds routed through the Swiss accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering / AML Breach in E-commerce Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Shopify store, PayPal and Stripe merchant accounts as a pass-through for third-party funds, issuing fictitious refunds to launder criminal proceeds, failing to implement basic KYC on high-volume cross-border transactions, or processing payments in an organised gang structure with fabricated customer data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Art. 305bis Swiss Criminal Code punishes money laundering with imprisonment of up to three years or a monetary penalty, and up to five years in aggravated cases. For gross negligence, the penalty is a fine of up to CHF 500,000. Under Art. 102 SCC, the company itself is liable to a fine of up to CHF 5 million where the offence was not prevented despite organisational measures, and all serviced assets may be confiscated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors found to have knowingly or negligently permitted laundering through the company's payment rails face criminal conviction, immediate passport confiscation and a global Interpol red notice, prohibition from practicing as directors, and personal confiscation of any ill-gotten gains. Civil liability to the damaged parties follows under the Swiss Code of Obligations with joinder of the estate.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-Deposit of Withholding Tax on Distributions / Veruntreuung
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The AG resolves a dividend to its non-resident owners but fails to withhold and deposit the 35% federal withholding tax within the statutory 30-day period, or deliberately mislabels a payment as a loan/royalty to avoid the withholding obligation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Statutory interest arrears of 4.5%–5% from the due date, penalty interest, a fine for gross negligence equal to 100% of the unpaid withholding tax, and criminal prosecution for 'Veruntreuung von Verrechnungssteuern' (Art. 186 DBG) punishable by imprisonment of up to three years and an additional fine. ESTV may issue a personal tax certificate against the responsible officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Art. 12 VStG expressly makes the members of the board of directors jointly, severally and unconditionally liable for the full amount of the unpaid withholding tax as a personal debt of the directors. Even after resignation, directors remain liable for tax amounts deposited or accrued during their term; bankruptcy of the AG does not extinguish the directors' personal liability; enforcement includes attachment of personal Swiss bank accounts and real estate.
